At this altar where the Holy Mother appeared alive, I thank the Holy Mother and Jesus a thousand times for allowing me to testify about a great healing in my life.
My name is Sister Stephna; I have been working in Germany for 15 years and I am a member of the MSMI congregation.
In 2022, I went to the gynecologist for a routine check-up.
During the check-up, the doctor said that a small cyst was seen on my ovary.
In the next check-up, they said both ovaries needed to be removed, so I was admitted to the hospital for a laparoscopy.
The day before I was admitted to the hospital was a Sunday, and I had work until Sunday afternoon.
After finishing work, I went and got admitted for the surgery scheduled on Monday, and they took me for the operation at 7 AM.
They told me the surgery would finish in 40 minutes and that I would be brought back to the room—to the intensive section—after the procedure.
But when I opened my eyes after the operation, it was around 12 noon, and I realized something else had happened.
The doctor came immediately and told me there was a large mass in my appendix and that the appendix was completely rotten, which they removed through laparoscopy.
But they saw a green-colored fluid in the peritoneum,
They said they could not remove it, and they sent all the operated cysts for biopsy; after being admitted for five days, I went home.
Four days after reaching home, my biopsy report came, and in the biopsy report I learned that the mass in the appendix was cancer.
Before this operation, it was only for the first time that I heard about Mother of Kreupasanam.
Even though I had taken a date for the surgery, all those days I worked with corona patients and cared for them.
I worked closely with people who had corona, yet I never got corona, but a day before fixing the first operation date, I got corona.
Because of that, my surgery was postponed; during that postponed period, one of our sisters called me as usual.
The sister called, spoke for a while, and after keeping the phone, within five minutes she called again.
The sister told me that when she entered the chapel after hanging up the phone, she felt someone telling her in her heart to tell Stephna about Kreupasanam.
Before the operation, the sister told me about this and said I should look at a website of Kreupasanam, and also there are many testimonies.
She told me to listen to them; although I had good faith in Mother Mary, I was never someone who believed in places of apparitions.
Nor was I someone who listened to many priests’ talks or believed in such things all these years.
But only because the sister told me, I watched the testimonies of Kreupasanam and listened to them, and after that, I went for this surgery.
In the hospital where I went for surgery, there was one of our own sisters too; she told me that whenever she went into the chapel, she felt someone telling her in her heart to tell Stephna about Kreupasanam,
and hearing that gave me a little more spiritual strength.
At that time, I started listening to more testimonies; after that, when I came to know that this appendix issue was cancer…
They had not confirmed that it started in the appendix; they did not know where the starting point was—only that the part removed from the appendix had cancer.
That was all they knew at that time, and for the next check-up I booked my ticket to travel to India.
I took an appointment at MVR Kozhikode Hospital for the evaluation.
At that time, one of my friends’ father, whose name was Father Bobby—he has now passed away— he told me,
“Why are you going now?” Father himself had fourth-stage cancer for four years and had received treatment in Germany.
His cancer was completely cured there, so Father said that if I go there from such a good medical facility,
it will be very difficult to adjust to the climate and other conditions.
Because Father insisted strongly, and after discussing with my provincial and general, I decided to continue the check-ups here itself.
By God’s special grace, I found a hospital just 10 minutes away from where we live, with a very good oncologist.
And the therapy they intended to give me—called HIPEC therapy—was also available in that hospital.
I still firmly believe that discovering that hospital was a powerful intervention of the Holy Mother.
During all this time of preparing for the operation, I listened to testimonies every single day.
During this period before the surgery, many people came to visit me, and all of them spoke to me about Kreupasanam.
So I began listening to even more testimonies.
Then the sisters told me that if someone from home goes and takes the Covenant, the Mother will surely intervene.
At that time only my nephew was at home; I have a younger brother.
He works in Africa, so I told my nephew that everyone was saying it would be good if someone could go to Kreupasanam.
Then my nephew told me, “Sister, the day I came to know you have cancer, I prayed to Mother like this.
I don’t have great faith, but if you come here, do the PET scan, and they say there is no cancer, I will take you there to give your testimony.”
The very next day after he prayed, a lady and a child came to our house; we had never seen them before, neither before nor after.
They drank some water at our house, gave us a Kreupasanam newsletter, and left.
From that day onward, my mother and my uncle—who earlier did not believe much in Kreupasanam— my brother,
my aunt, all of them together started waking up at 5:30 to pray the Apparition Prayer.
After that, I was going for my surgery; my open surgery was scheduled for November 22, 2022.
Two or three days before going for the open surgery, I remembered how in the testimonies everyone mentioned having the blessed salt or oil or other offerings from Kreupasanam.
But as someone working in Germany, I had no way of getting any such items. So on the day before I went for the operation,
A sister whom I did not know at all called me; I had no prior familiarity with her.
She told me that she had gone to India recently and had brought blessed salt and honey from Kreupasanam, and that if I wanted it, she could not bring it herself, but someone could come and take it.
So the sister who was staying with me went and brought the salt and honey; holding the salt in my hand, I went for the operation that day.
Just before the operation, I put a few grains of the salt into my hand, and then I went for the surgery.
Before the operation, I fully believed that when the doctor opened my abdomen, they would find nothing wrong and would immediately close it—that they would finish the surgery quickly.
They had told me the operation would take six hours, but when it was over, it had lasted nine and a half hours.
After that, according to what they said, I was supposed to stay in the intensive ICU for four days.
But when I opened my eyes in the ICU, I saw myself talking to one of my friends about Mother Kreupasanam.
The moment I woke up, I immediately asked the doctor standing near me what had happened to me.
When I heard what the doctor said, I was shocked, because inside my abdomen, they had…
I am saying all this only to show what a great miracle happened—they removed a part of my small intestine.
A portion of the large intestine that had moved upward, and a bottle-like structure inside our abdomen through which things pass—they completely removed that too.
My uterus, bladder—almost all the organs in my abdomen—had cancer cells spread on them.
They removed all of that, and that is why the surgery took so long.
Before the operation, the only thing I prayed for—the one thing I desired— Since I am a nurse,
I know all the complications, so my first prayer was that only the bottle inside my abdomen that needs to be removed,
whatever else they remove, I have no problem—that was my only concern from the beginning.
After all this, I thought I had prayed foolishly to Mother of Kreupasanam,
I wondered whether, because I prayed like that and believed like that, Mother allowed all these complications to happen.
But from that very moment, my recovery amazed all the doctors, nurses, and everyone who cared for me.
They said I should stay in the ICU for four days, but after one and a half days, I got up from the ICU bed myself and moved to another bed, so they shifted me to a normal room.
The doctor who operated on me used to come every morning at seven o’clock before changing his scrubs to check on me.
The doctor said he had never seen such a big miracle in his life—someone recovering this fast after such a huge surgery.
From the second day onward, I slowly started walking.
Even after removing so many parts of my body in the surgery, I never had any major difficulty; only slight issues with food in the beginning.
But I never had any serious complications.
Then, on December 23rd—exactly one month later—the bottle or bag which I disliked and never wanted was removed, and everything became normal.
During all these days, many people offered Holy Mass for me and prayed for me.
Especially in all the convents of our province, Holy Mass was offered every day for me.
It is the great miracle and intercession of the Holy Mass and the Holy Mother that has helped me stand before you today to give this testimony.
After that, exactly three months later, I returned to India; I came home, and from home I came here.
I came here to attend the training and had no problems, but at that time I could not stand for long, so I could not give my testimony or take the Covenant.
Today is the first time I am taking the Covenant, and through this I have been able to grow spiritually in many ways.
I was able to read the Holy Scripture more, place greater trust in Mother Mary, and draw closer to Jesus.
A thousand thanks to the Mother and the Holy Son who gave me so many blessings;
2 Samuel 22:7, “In my distress I called upon the Lord.” “I cried to my God for help; from His temple He heard my voice, and my cry reached His ears.”
Sister Stephna shared with us the entire mountain of suffering she went through in her life, but not as a story of sorrow or weakness in illness.
Rather, she shared how Mother Kreupasanam intervened at the right time in this daughter’s life— and how through many people,
through the experiences of many children who took the Covenant, the presence and protection of the Mother came to her.
With inner courage and deep trust in God, holding close to her heart the blessed articles of Mother Kreupasanam,
she went forward into those major surgeries—surgeries for which doctors had written a verdict that could lead even to death
and could leave her life in a miserable and helpless condition; but Time-shortening Mother Help washed her with the precious blood of Jesus,
purified her, healed her internal organs, and restored her completely—this is the testimony she shared at this altar.
Sister is someone whose digestive system organs and reproductive organs—almost all of them—were removed entirely from her body.
And because of that, at such a young age, her long journey ahead—her entire future—could have turned into a painful and tragic path.
Sister mentioned only a very small part of it at this altar; if she were to narrate everything in detail, she wonders whether it could even be completed.
Because as I read this testimony paper here, I understand how painful the days she lived through were—
days when she had no hope and not even a desire to continue life.
Yet at every moment, just as we call Mother Kreupasanam the “Pilgrim Mother,” she came to each one through various people, telling them about Kreupasanam,
inviting them to trust in the Mother, to pray, to participate in the Covenant testimonies and Covenant meditations, constantly helping them.
Throughout her sickness bed, giving her spiritual courage, hope, and the strongest inner strength to surrender all her suffering to Jesus
and to offer herself completely to the treatment—this was all made possible by the hopeful prayers she made to Mother Kreupasanam, as she herself testifies.
Unexpectedly hearing about Kreupasanam first through others, the sisters calling and mentioning it; the sister who first called and hung up,
then calling again to speak about Kreupasanam; another person she hardly knew saying she had Kreupasanam salt and honey in her hands,
and that if someone came, she could give it, because she herself could not go there—yet it reached her hands exactly when she longed and prayed for it.
While praying and desiring for such things in those moments, she received knowledge about them; and after the operation, she prayed that she should not have to carry the colostomy bag her whole life,
praying that such misery should not be given to her; and the first thing she checked in those difficult moments after surgery was whether that colostomy bag was there.
Seeing the colostomy bag, she was completely shattered, and with a broken heart she prayed to the Mother.
The Mother, seeing those tears and that brokenness, began healing her more rapidly from that very moment, restoring everything to normal in a short time and giving her recovery.
It was such an extraordinary healing that even the doctor testified that in his career he had never seen a surgery like this, a healing like this, or someone returning to full health like this.
Dear ones, when we call upon the Mother and pray, the Mother stands with us and obtains blessings from Jesus for us.
No matter how much suffering we go through, no matter how shattered our lives may seem, even when we feel we have no hope at all,
if we surrender ourselves into the hands of the Mother, for the world to acknowledge the apparition, for the Church to accept it,
she works through miraculous signs and wondrous deeds; I am living even today because of that.
Just as at Cana she told the disciples to do whatever He tells them—and the water became wine—so too in the sufferings of life, I will continue to work in the world as a testimony for the glory of God.
That is the testimony Sister shared at this altar.
Let us give thanks to the Mother and to Jesus for the health, healing, and spiritual enlightenment Sister received, and offer this testimony with a clap of hands.
